entities.name: Jacob Cornelisz. van Neck
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jacob Corneliszoon van Neck was a Dutch naval officer and explorer who led the second Dutch expedition to Indonesia from 1598 to 1599. 


 This expedition, which took place during the Dutch Golden Age, was instrumental in expanding Dutch trade and colonial influence in Southeast Asia. The expedition's success was largely due to van Neck's navigational skills and his ability to establish relationships with local leaders. 


 As a result of this expedition, the Dutch East India Company was able to establish a permanent presence in Indonesia, which would go on to play a significant role in shaping the country's history. 


 Despite the significance of this expedition, van Neck's contributions were largely overlooked until recent historical research brought his achievements to light. 


 As a testament to his enduring legacy, van Neck's name remains synonymous with Dutch exploration and colonization in Indonesia.
